title: James Bond Comic Book Series in the Works from Grant Morrison, IDW (Exclusive)
full_text: × Skip to main content By Borys Kit Plus Icon Borys Kit Senior Film Writer View All October 9, 2026 9:00am 007 Logo and Grant Morrison Allan Amato Logo text IDW Publishing has acquired the license to thrill and has set Morrison, Grant Morrison , to shake, not stir, things up. Partnering with Ian Fleming Publications, IDW has picked up the license to create all-new comic book adventures featuring the iconic British spy James Bond . The two companies have tapped writer Grant Morrison, the influential and award-winning scribe known for All-Star Superman and his multi-year Batman run as well medium-pushing comics such as Animal Man and Doom Patrol . Related Stories Movies Saoirse Ronan Responds to Rumors That Husband Jack Lowden Will Be the Next James Bond TV Pierce Brosnan and Helen Mirren on Their 'MobLand' Season 2 Return: "Pure Lunacy" “Pairing a renowned franchise like James Bond with the visionary writer Grant Morrison is a perfect example of IDW doing what it does best with licensed properties,” said IDW CEO Davidi Jonas in a statement to The Hollywood Reporter. “Our goal isn’t to simply provide supplemental and optional stories. We strive to take radical swings which celebrate and stay true to the very qualities that make the franchise special while also reinventing it for the modern comic book landscape.” Stated Morrison, “I’ve been a James Bond fan for as long as I can remember and this opportunity to put my own stamp on a British character as iconic as King Arthur, Robin Hood or Sherlock Holmes, was too good to miss.” The comic has no artist on board yet nor does it have a release date. It does, however, have a title for its six-part opening adventure: Sunbreaker . (That is not, however, the title of the comic, which remains at this time for their eyes only.) Morrison is promising new cars, new gadgets, and a new ultimate villain ripped straight from the headlines. “Our opening 6-part adventure, Sunbreaker , attempts to create a definitive Bond story featuring everything fans love about the character and his world, while adding a whole lot more,” Morrison said. “Expect to see James Bond in a few unfamiliar situations, facing unfamiliar foes, in a world very like our own as reflected in a deadly funhouse mirror – a world of intrigue, violence, double cross and deception. A world through which James Bond glides like a killer shark among minnows. Charismatic, ruthless, unstoppable.” A fictional British spy hero, Bond, also known as 007, made his debut in the 1953 with the Ian Fleming-written novel Casino Royale . The first movie, Dr. No , was released in 1962 and starred Sean Connery. Bond movies have been a regular pop culture event since then, with now 25 outings in the film series with another one due to begin production next year. The character’s appearance in comics has been sporadic. Marvel did adaptations of the Roger Moore entries For Your Eyes Only and Octopussy in the early 1980s and new adventures have come in bits, fits and starts since 1989, initially from Eclipse Comics and later from Dark Horse Comics and Dynamite Comics. The license is coup for IDW, which also publishes a slew of Star Trek comics. “James Bond is a character with an incredible legacy across books, films, video games and comics,” said Ian Fleming Publications publishing director Simon Ward. “At Ian Fleming Publications we are always looking for the best medium for each Bond story and there are some adventures that can only be told through comics. The team at IDW wowed us with their vision for the future of 007 original comics and as someone who has been reading Grant Morrison for many years, I think we’re in for something new and very special.” THR

title: ‘Trust Me, I’m a Doctor’ Review: Kal Penn Plays Anna Nicole Smith’s Physician in a Moldy and Misguided Bio-Dramedy
full_text: × Skip to main content By Frank Scheck Plus Icon Frank Scheck View All October 9, 2026 9:00am 'Trust Me, I'm a Doctor' Briarcliff Entertainment It would have seemed safe to assume that public interest in anything related to Anna Nicole Smith has long since passed its sell-by date. But apparently not to the makers of the too-cutely titled new film about the legal travails of Smith’s former doctor, Sandeep Kapoor, who was charged with multiple crimes related to his treatment of the reality TV star after her 2007 death from a drug overdose at age 39. Based on Kapoor’s self-published memoir (that should have been a clue), Trust Me, I’m a Doctor feels like it’s arriving nearly two decades too late. Written and directed by Thane Economou — whose sole previous feature credit, 2016’s The Wedding Party , is described in the press notes as “a rom-com filmed in one continuous 119-minute take” — the movie stars Kal Penn as the unfortunate doctor who got a bit carried away with his colorful new patient, played by Abbie Cornish ( Bright Star ). He became her friend and confidant, seduced by her fame and lifestyle. Attempting to explain himself, he asks, “Have you ever walked on a red carpet?” Related Stories News TMZ's Harvey Levin Cut Kanye West's Hitler Praise From 2018 Interview, Former Staffer Says Business Harvey Levin's Next TMZ Overhaul: True-Crime, With a Dash of Populism Trust Me, I'm a Doctor The Bottom Line Oy! Release date : Friday, October 16 Cast : Kal Penn, Linda Hamilton, David Julian Harish, Abbie Cornish Director-screenwriter : Thane Economou Rated R, 1 hour 51 minutes Kapoor was often photographed with her at various events and parties, most notably when he rode in her limo as part of a West Hollywood gay pride parade. Beginning the story with a depiction of the police raid on Kapoor’s home that feels more than a little exaggerated in its rabid intensity, the story flashes back to chronicle his relationship with his patient as related during a discovery session with his attorney Ellyn Garofalo (a fine Linda Hamilton ). Economou frequently adopts a decidedly jokey approach, as if he’s aware that it would be hard to take seriously this story involving such outlandish real-life figures as Smith; photographer Larry Birkhead (Ted Jefferies), who filed a paternity suit against her over her daughter Dannielynn; Howard K. Stern (David Julian Hirsh), her lawyer, who co-starred with her in a reality TV show and who also claimed he was Dannielynn’s father; and Harvey Levin (Elon Gold), the founder of TMZ . Penn’s Kapoor narrates the proceedings, often breaking the fourth wall to address us directly. A tired running gag involves Stern’s name (“no, the other one,” characters point out to separate him from the radio show host). Unfortunately, the film lacks the wit that made such similarly stylized true-life films as The Big Short so effective. It’s also very clunky, with background information ladled out via such things as fake TMZ segments and lawyer/client “sidebars” with all the finesse of Wikipedia entries. The tone is maddeningly inconsistent, straining for heartfelt emotion through such maudlin plot elements as Kapoor’s relationship with his parents, who were unaware that he was gay, and his friendship with a dying elderly female patient. The whole story is so bizarre — the segment about Prince Frederic von Anhalt, Zsa Zsa Gabor’s ninth husband, who also claimed to be the father of Smith’s child, could easily be expanded into a feature film itself — that it exerts a certain morbid fascination. But the most interesting character onscreen, Smith, is given short shrift, despite a worthy performance by Cornish, in favor of concentrating on Kapoor, about whom it’s hard to care much about. And though Penn delivers a sensitive turn as the doctor so desperate for attention and validation that he made terrible mistakes in judgment, he’s unable to make the film feel like anything other than yet another sleazy attempt to capitalize on Smith’s notoriety. Full credits Production: Picture Movers, Stadium, RBF Productions Films, Good Good Films, Low Road Films, Spy Films Distributor: Briarcliff Entertainment Cast: Kal Penn, Linda Hamilton, David Julian Harish, Abbie Cornish Director-screenwriter: Thane Economou Producers: Ryan Hawkins, Al Engelmann, Rebecca Case, Geenah Krisht Executive producers: Kal Penn, Thane Economou, David Gale, Charlotte Ubben, Randy Wooten, Melora Donoghue, Nashwa & Ali Krisht, Michael Lazari, Tom Ortenberg Director of photography: Bobby Shore Production designer: Melanie Garros Editor: Brian Berdan Composers: Daniel Stockdale, Niles Hollowell-Dhar Costume designer: Hanna Puley Casting: Anne McCarthy, Kellie Roy, Morgan Robbins, Stephanie Gorin Rated R, 1 hour 51 minutes THR

title: Netflix’s ‘Little House On The Prairie’ Season 2 Casts Peter Ingalls, Mrs. Nelson & More As Production Wraps
full_text: Skip to main content By Dessi Gomez Dessi Gomez SEO Staff Writer @GomezDessi More Stories By Dessi Owen Wilson’s Pryce Cahill Makes Play At U.S. Open In ‘Stick’ Season 2 Trailer All The Songs In ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 So Far ‘Ted Lasso’ Season 4 Finale Recap: The Last Match Of The Season & A Shareholders’ Showdown View All October 9, 2026 9:00am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Clockwise from top left: David Wronko, Elyse Levesque, Erik Althavale, Graham Harvey, Jacinta Forest Lewitski, Lyla Porter-Follows, Martin Roach, Paul Greene, Ryan Northcott and Scott Porter Cameron Radice/Jenna Berman/Kevin McIntyre/Monica Gosselin/Benjamin Laird/Sarah Jane Murray/Time Leyes/Laurent Levy/Kevin Clarke/Malik Daniels The second season of Netflix ’s Little House on the Prairie reimagining has rounded out its ensemble cast with a wrap on production. Ten names have boarded Season 2: David Wronko , Erik Athaval ( American Hostage ), Elyse Levesque ( Ready or Not, Orphan Black ), Graham Harvey ( The Night Agent ), Jacinta Forest Lewitski , Lyla Porter-Follows ( High Potential ), Martin Roach ( Cross ), Paul Greene ( When Calls The Heart, Autumn and the Black Jaguar ), Ryan Northcott ( Anna Pigeon) and Scott Porter ( Ginny & Georgia, Friday Night Lights, Hart of Dixie ). Related Stories Casting Rachelle Lefevre & Charlotte Sullivan Join ‘Little House On The Prairie’ Season 2 At Netflix Books Everything We Know About Netflix’s ‘Little House On The Prairie’ Season 2 So Far Athavale will portray energetic minister Reverend Alden, who leads Walnut Grove’s Congregational church. Levesque will play Emma Perry, wife of Luther Perry and mother to Maud and Thomas, who secretly calls the shots for her husband’s business. Harvey will play Johnny Johnson, son of Norwegian immigrants and farm boy who has never attended school. Lewitski will play Hannah Walker, Lena Nelson’s farm manager, who is part Dakota and plays first base for the Prairie Clippers. Porter Follows will portray Mrs. Lena Nelson, an outspoken young widow in charge of the farm her husband left behind. Watch on Deadline Roach will portray civil war veteran Simon Hughes, a widower who owns the Blacksmith Shop. Greene will play Luther Perry, husband to Emma Perry and father of Thomas and Maud. Luther is a grain buyer and town baker who poses a threat to the farmers. Northcott will play William Oleson, husband to Margaret Oleson (Charlotte Sullivan) and father to Nellie Oleson (Willa Dunn). And, last but not least, Porter will portray Uncle Peter, older brother to Charles aka “Pa” Ingalls (Luke Bracey) All but Porter’s are recurring guest stars. Uncle Peter is a guest star role in the second season. L-R: Skywalker Hughes as Mary Ingalls, Alice Halsey as Laura Ingalls behind the scenes of episode 207 of ‘Little House on the Prairie’ Eric Zachanowich/Netflix In On the Banks of Plum Creek , Mrs. Nelson is married to a Mr. Nelson, and both are Norwegian neighbors to the Ingalls in their new home in Minnesota. They share a daughter named Anna. Pa also works for Mr. Nelson in Laura Ingalls Wilder’s novel. Mixing hopeful family drama and survival tale suspense, Little House on the Prairie tells the story of one family’s adventure and origin story settling the American West. It is based on Wilder’s semi-autobiographical book series. Rebecca Sonnenshine ( The Boys, Vampire Diaries, Archive 81) serves as showrunner and executive producer. Executive producers include Joy Gorman Wedtels for Joy Coalition, Trip Friendly for Friendly Family Productions, Dana Fox and Pascal Verschooris, who also directs the Season 2 finale episode. More directors include Kat Candler (201), Kyle Patrick Alvarez (202), Julie Anne Robinson (203), Liza Johnson (204), Sarah Boyd (205), Ellen Kuras (206) and Sydney Freeland (207), The adaptation is produced by CBS Studios and Anonymous Content Studio.

title: ‘Star Wars: Galactic Racer’ Debuts on Amazon Luna Day and Date With Wide Release (Gaming News Roundup)
full_text: Oct 9, 2026 8:53am PT ‘Star Wars: Galactic Racer’ Debuts on Amazon Luna Day and Date With Wide Release (Gaming News Roundup) By Isabelle Farina , Tanya Fedak Fuse Games “ Star Wars: Galactic Racer ” launched on Amazon’s gaming service Luna day and date alongside the game’s worldwide release across platforms including PlayStation 5, Xbox Series S and X and PC. Developed by Fuse Games, the studio behind the “Burnout” and “Need for Speed” franchises, “Star Wars: Galactic Racer” puts players behind the controls of a range of repulsorcraft in a racing circuit in a galaxy far, far away. Related Stories ‘Bowie80’ to Celebrate David Bowie’s 80th Birthday With Events, Exhibits, Releases and More Throughout 2027 A Rare David Bowie Self-Portrait — Featuring His Handprints — Is Going on Auction at Sotheby's Set early during the New Republic era, the game introduces the Galactic League, an unsanctioned racing circuit assembled by Darius Pax. Players step into the role of Shade, a lone racer dreaming of glory and revenge. The high-stakes racing takes place across “Star Wars” planets like Jakku, the Graveyard of Giants, Ando Prime or Sentinel I. Popular on Variety “We’ve always believed Luna players deserve to be in the action from day one, and Star Wars: Galactic Racer makes that a reality for the first time,” said Jeff Gattis, head of gaming at Amazon. “Luna players can jump into the single-player campaign today without needing to own a console or wait for a lengthy download. And the best part: if they’re a Prime member, they already have it at no additional cost. It’s exactly the kind of experience we want to deliver on Luna, and we think players are going to love it.” Prime members can start their engines on Amazon Luna on the same day as other platforms and play the single-player campaign. See more gaming news from the week in the roundup below. PARTNERSHIPS/COLLABS Zara Larsson is collaborating with Winx Club for a limited-edition card from trading card brand Kayou. Dressed in her outfit from the “Midnight Sun” music video, the card features Larsson posing alongside the Winx Club fairies. The collaboration will debut at New York Comic Con, which begins Thursday and goes until Sunday. Kayou will also offer cards featuring “KPop Demon Hunters,” “My Little Pony” and “Monster Jam” at this year’s comic con. * Discord is teaming up with The Living Tombstone on an original Halloween track and a Halloween remix of the Discord ringtone. The Living Tombstone’s new original track, “Don’t Hang Up the Call” and accompanying video are inspired by the quirks of how people actually spend time together on “Discord.” The Living Tombstone is putting its own spin on Discord’s iconic ringtone for the season. The Living Tombstone’s have turned gaming and internet fandom into music inspired by the games and culture their fans love. Over 30 million users take part in personal, gaming and interest-based servers each month, including 7.2 million in music communities. NEWLY ANNOUNCED GAMES During RuneFest 2026 over the weekend, developer Jagex announced new content coming to “RuneScape,” “Old School RuneScape” and “RuneScape: Dragonwilds,” as well as an upcoming fourth “RuneScape” MMO game. Still early in development, the as-yet-unnamed title will “bring the world of Gielinor to life in Unreal Engine, combining the depth, freedom and community-led spirit that have defined RuneScape for 25 years with the technology and game design possibilities of today,” per the team. “RuneScape Reignited” launches Dec. 2, inviting players old and new to return together and rediscover “RuneScape” with the ultimate RuneScape experience. Players can get full Reignited Access without a membership from Dec. 2 to Dec. 12. The Plugin API is launching in October, with players getting an early hands-on ahead of official release. “Hoard of Dragons” kicks off in January, offering a sequel to the popular “Dragon Slayer” quest, “City of Gnomes” continues the gnome storyline, first stated in 2002 and “Secrets of Karamja” introduces a new end game raid. These arcs weave together “RuneScape”’s 2027 content into three distinct story narratives and also include an agility skill rework, new skilling and solo bosses, new area expansions and a new “Grandmaster Quest.” “Luminance,” a brand-new update serving as a prelude to 2027’s “Blood Crystal Saga,” launches in December this year, and features the introduction of the Elves into “RuneScape: Dragonwilds,” new elven-themed customisation options for player characters and buildings alike and the Prayer skill. “The Blood Crystal Saga” kicks off in 2027 starting with the Song of Rebellion in early 2027. Official modding arrives on “Dragonwilds” in 2027 through a new partnership with CurseForge. * Step into the castle! “The Traitors ” fans can now test their scheming skills with “The Traitors: Interactive Game” on iOS and Android platforms, Fusebox Games announced on Monday. Players begin by choosing a defining trait: the outspoken leader, the adaptable chameleon or the chaotic wildcard, which will form the foundation of your character. Set across 12 days, 22 players emulate the TV show at the castle by building trust with other players during missions as well as building believable theories during The Round Table. “When it comes to adapting iconic entertainment IP, Fusebox Games is as faithful a partner as they come,” Fusebox Games CEO Terry Lee said. “Our history is built on story-based, choice-driven games that put players in control, making the deceit and strategy of The Traitors a natural fit. We’re giving fans the chance to step out of the audience and take a seat at the table and tell their own story at the castle.” TECH Google is introducing “Playground,” an experimental gaming platform that lets users create, play and share fully custom games with no coding experience required. With “Playground”’s conversational interface, users can create custom games by typing what they want, remixing starter prompts or getting guided support to help them share their creativity with the world. Users can refine the rules with prompts, customize characters and tweak the environment until it’s what they envision. “Playground” is browser-based, games are playable across phones and laptops. Once a game is ready, users have the option to keep their game private, generate a shareable link to send to friends and family or publish it to share with the broader “Playground” community. Since “Playground” supports multiplayer gameplay, gamers can also see in-game leaderboards and follow other creators to see their latest creations. The upcoming “Unity Spark Integration: Playground” will soon offer integration with UnitySpark so creators who want to expand their concepts can take advantage of Unity Spark’s robust, professional-level mechanics, 3-D capabilities and the flexibility of the Unity runtime. GAMES UPDATES Gamers, your vocabulary just got a whole lot bigger. “Words With Friends” has added 25,000 new playable words, modernized definitions and a word-reporting tool that gives the community a direct role in shaping the game’s official dictionary. The new words reflect popular culture terms, lifestyle words and slang like buzzworthy, bff, drip, and bookclub. “We are constantly listening to our players and working to give them the best experience, and our players made it clear – they wanted new words, modern definitions, and a dictionary that evolves alongside them,” Yaron Leyvand, Executive Vice President, Mobile Games, Zynga said. “This update delivers on that promise. Words With Friends has always been about connection, and language is at the heart of that. We’re thrilled to finally give players an expansive dictionary that matches the way they speak, play, and connect today.” The updated dictionary is available now in Words With Friends. Players can download Words With Friends for free on the App Store, Google Play, and WordsWithFriends.com. title: Mike Ditka, Legendary Chicago Bears Coach and Football Analyst, Dies at 86
full_text: Oct 9, 2026 8:50am PT Mike Ditka, Legendary Chicago Bears Coach and Football Analyst, Dies at 86 By William Earl Plus Icon William Earl @beautifulbill Latest Mike Ditka, Legendary Chicago Bears Coach and Football Analyst, Dies at 86 11 minutes ago Shudder Acquires Supernatural Horror Film ‘Split Rock’ Ahead of World Premiere at Sitges (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago Lucio Fulci’s ‘The Beyond’ Set for Remake; Hangtime International Pictures and Severin Films Forge Partnership for More Genre Reboots (EXCLUSIVE) 1 day ago See All Getty Images Mike Ditka , the iconic football player, Chicago Bears coach and football analyst, died at 86 years old, his family announced. ESPN was the first to report the news . No cause of death was revealed. Ditka’s larger-than-life personality made him a celebrity in the ’80s as he coached the 1985 Bears to their only Super Bowl win. He was fired by the Bears in 1992, and after some time off, coached the New Orleans Saints for three seasons. Related Stories A Rare David Bowie Self-Portrait — Featuring His Handprints — Is Going on Auction at Sotheby's ‘Bowie80’ to Celebrate David Bowie’s 80th Birthday With Events, Exhibits, Releases and More Throughout 2027 After coaching, Ditka became an analyst at NBC and later ESPN. He was a fixture on ESPN’s “Sunday Morning Countdown” from 2006 to 2015. Popular on Variety “It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather and friend, Mike Ditka,” his family shared in a statement. “While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.” Ditka was born on Oct. 18, 1939, in Aliquippa, Pennsylvania and started his pro football career in the NFL after college at Pitt. He was a tight end who was drafted in 1961 by the Bears and won Rookie of the Year. He played six years in Chicago, followed by two for the Philadelphia Eagles and then four playing for the Dallas Cowboys. title: The Netflix Ax Is Coming as Stock Languishes
full_text: × Skip to main content By Erik Hayden , Borys Kit October 9, 2026 8:44am Co-CEO of Netflix Ted Sarandos speaks during the Bloomberg Screentime 2026 conference in Los Angeles, on September 30, 2026. Patrick T. Fallon / AFP via Getty Images For weeks there’s been a steady drumbeat near the halls of power at Netflix over the question of rightsizing, job cuts and a restructure ahead of its third quarter earnings disclosure on October 20. While the streaming giant still lords over its rivals in the subscription space and co-chiefs Ted Sarandos and Greg Peters command an annual content spending budget of $20 billion, Wall Street arguably has viewed this as an off year for Netflix. Once a high-flying tech growth story, the nearly 30-year-old company is now the studio establishment as all the attention and investment has gone to AI bets in public markets. The company also has had to fight off an ever-growing YouTube, which is increasingly becoming the dominant platform on TV screens in addition to its video lead on mobile devices. With stock down 20 percent year to date, Sarandos and Peters may unveil a shake up that could be geared in part to showing the Street that it’s ready to accelerate growth in the post-Streaming Wars economy. In the last several weeks, multiple journalists have been hearing that cuts could be in the 5 percent range, or more, at the company. The Hollywood Reporter has been hearing the same from sources about upcoming belt-tightening, and Sarandos himself has been laying those expectations in public settings as well. The company has 16,000 employees, 10,900 of which are based in the U.S., as of the company’s last 10-K filing in December. A reorganization may be undertaken in the next few months. Netflix declined to comment on Friday. “Overall, we’re not growing as fast as I want us to, and we’re working on making that move faster,” the co-CEO said at Bloomberg‘s Screentime event on Sept. 30, in a nod to the potential rework to come. He also added, “The business is great and growing fine.” Netflix regularly cuts staff and rehires, that’s been a principle from founder Reed Hastings he even wrote about in his 2020 book, No Rules Rules: Netflix and the Culture of Reinvention . But these pink slips would mark more of a significant mass restructure should they come to pass. Layoffs, if strategically executed with a go-forward plan, can sometimes help boost share price and Wall Street has been valuing austerity at the top publicly traded companies for several years now. The move would be in keeping with layoff season at the other Hollywood majors. Disney, under new CEO Josh D’Amaro, has been in the middle of his first notable round of pink slips while Warner Bros. and Paramount will soon see the ax fall as well as the Skydance team searches for $6 billion in synergies. THR

title: Focus Features & Blumhouse-Atomic Monster Snap Up Micro-Budget Horror Film ‘Play House’ From Nicolas Curcio
full_text: Skip to main content By Matt Grobar Matt Grobar Senior Film Reporter More Stories By Matt Robby Hoffman Sets Second Netflix Special Paramount Teaming With Medieval Times On Family Comedy Movie; Eric Appel Directing From Script By Blaise Hemingway Paul Walter Hauser Set For Crime Drama ‘Garden City’ From John Curran, Magenta Light Studios View All October 9, 2026 8:31am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Nicolas Curcio Gilbert Flores/Getty Images EXCLUSIVE: Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster have snapped up Play House , a micro-budget horror film from Nicolas Curcio , in a competitive situation, sources tell Deadline. We’re told this was a seven-figure deal for worldwide rights, excluding Latin America and India. This is a major coup for Curcio’s debut feature, a film made for not much more than $100,000 — roughly 13% of the reported budget of Curry Barker’s low-budget Focus phenomenon Obsession . Related Stories News Top 50 Halloween Movies Photo Gallery: Creepy Classics From ‘Psycho,’ ‘The Shining’ To ‘Obsession’ & ‘Get Out’ News Horror Movies’ Next Wave: What’s Coming In 2026, From Auteur Nightmares To Indie Breakouts Curcio set the project in motion last September after winning the inaugural Fantastic Pitches contest, a micro-budget genre initiative spearheaded by Alamo Drafthouse’s Fantastic Fest and indie studio Chroma, thereby securing funding and distribution. He returned to Fantastic Fest to premiere the film last month. Play House will release in theaters in 2027, with Universal Pictures International handling international distribution. Watch on Deadline Written by Curcio and wife/creative partner Kirby Gladstein, the film follows Elliott (Will Harrison), who while renovating a dilapidated house to win back his ex, discovers VHS tapes of an unaired children’s TV show which begins to seep into his life, threatening his last chance at reconciliation. Pic’s cast also includes Jessica Sula, Jordan Gonzalez, and James Urbaniak. Curcio and Gladstein produced for Skinny Ghost, alongside Ben Gojer, Jack Forbes, and Derek Tramont. Exec producers include Ahbra Perry via Chroma, Daniel Levin via Narrative, Adam Hendricks and Greg Gilreath of Divide/Conquer, and Jason Blum of Blumhouse Atomic-Monster. NPerry repped the film for sales via Narrative Distribution. While Universal art-house label Focus Features has not historically been known as a major horror distributor, outside of recent work with Robert Eggers on titles like Nosferatu and the upcoming Werwulf , they’re now aggressively expanding into the space as supporters of emerging filmmakers, after seeing Obsession break out as their highest-grossing film ever at over $522M worldwide. Divide/Conquer’s Hendricks and Gilreath — EPs on Play House — previously brought that film to Blum, who set it up at Focus, along with his follow-up Anything but Ghosts , dated for May 7, 2027. You can expect much more to come from the collaboration between Focus Features and Blumhouse-Atomic Monster. Most recently, they announced their partnership on director Josh Giuliano’s Occupant following the buzzy TIFF debut of his first horror film, River . Curcio is a rising filmmaker who recently set up his high-concept thriller spec Sweet Spot , penned with Gladstein, at Paramount Primal, as we first reported. A writer on Sony Pictures Animation’s hit GOAT , he has developed projects for multiple studios, including a live-action Magic School Bus for Universal and an adaptation of Planet of the Nerds for Paramount. His script Barron made the Black List in 2019. Curcio is also known for running a popular screenwriting TikTok account with nearly 200K followers and over 10M likes, and has partnered with studios like Neon, A24 and Paramount to promote films. He is repped by 3 Arts, UTA, and Jackoway Austen Tyerman. title: Rachel Stockman Succeeds Dan Abrams as CEO of Law&Crime and Court TV
full_text: × Skip to main content By Tony Maglio Plus Icon Tony Maglio View All October 9, 2026 8:31am Rachel Stockman and Dan Abrams Courtesy; Dave Kotinsky/Getty Images Rachel Stockman has been named CEO of Law&Crime and Court TV , replacing Dan Abrams in title. Stockman had previously served as president; Abrams will remain with the company as chairman. Abrams had a three-year earn out from when he sold the Law&Crime business, The Hollywood Reporter has learned. That period just ended; Abrams sold Law&Crime for $130 million. Law&Crime has a large online presence in the true crime and legal content spaces. Law&Crime has four FAST channels, millions of YouTube subscribers, billions of video views and more than 700 million hours watched across platforms over the past year, the brand says. Law&Crime acquired Court TV from Scripps in 2026. Just last month, Law&Crime signed with WME for representation, as first reported by THR . Stockman recently oversaw the launch of “Partners in Crime,” a programming initiative featuring six original series developed with popular true-crime creators. Stockman has executive produced dozens of documentaries and series for Netflix, Paramount+, A&E, Fox Nation and ID/HBO Max. “Rachel’s ability to direct the business at the highest level while also making so many smart, granular decisions has helped lead us to where we are today,” Abrams, founder and chairman of Law&Crime and Court TV, said in a statement. “She has truly earned this. I can’t wait to see where she takes us next.” “I’m incredibly proud of our extraordinary team and everything we’ve accomplished together,” said Stockman. “I’m honored to lead this next chapter as we continue to push boundaries, embrace bold ideas and help shape the future of media.” THR profiled Abrams in May . The former court reporter will be plenty busy even with a more passive role at Law&Crime/Court TV. Abrams also serves as chief legal analyst at ABC News, founder and CEO of website Mediaite, host of SiriusXM radio series The Dan Abrams Show (SiriusXM POTUS) and host and exec producer of the cable series Court Cam (A&E) and On Patrol: Live (Reelz). Abrams even owns a winery (Ev&Em) and a Rotten Tomatoes-for-booze company The Daily Pour, as well as popular New York City restaurant Danny’s. In his nonexistent down time, Abrams writes books — he’s actively working on Scars, Sanity and a Six-Pack at 60 , which is due out in January from Simon & Schuster. THR

title: The Most Powerful Women in International TV
full_text: × Skip to main content Illustrated by Pixel Pusher As the global television industry heads to Cannes for MIPCOM, which runs Oct. 12-15, scale has become the sector’s answer to survival. Comcast’s Sky has agreed to buy ITV’s broadcasting and streaming businesses for 1.6 billion pounds ($2.12 billion), while Banijay’s $8 billion megamerger with All3Media has created an (even larger) indie production and distribution colossus. But these deals are a response to something bigger: a business whose traditional models, built on linear schedules, scripted dramas and predictable ad revenues, are being upended by streaming, vertical dramas and AI’s ability to automate parts of the creative process. Related Stories Movies U.K. Box Office Back to Full Health -- But What Lessons Do We Learn? Business Skydance's Gerhard Zeiler, Warner Bros. Int'l President, to Depart With Eyes on Politics THR For the women on THR ‘s 2026 list of the Most Powerful Women in International Television, the challenge is to adapt to technological disruption without losing what makes the work worth watching. “You’ve got to continue to invest in AI,” says ITV chief Carolyn McCall, who negotiated the Sky deal. “You’ve got to continue to invest in efficiency, and most importantly, you’ve got to have enough money to constantly invest in content, because content is where it’s at. That’s what makes you all your money.” It’s a sentiment — lean into the technology but keep a focus on the creative — echoed by the execs across this list. Rai Fiction’s Maria Pia Ammirati cautions against “the increasing tendency to delegate creative processes to technology,” while Renata Brandão of Brazil’s Conspiração Filmes wants the industry to trust “producers, creators and instinct over predictive metrics.” Selections were based on an executive’s decision-making authority — the ability to greenlight, commission or finance content — combined with the impact and performance of their work over the past 12 months. Mo Abudu CEO, EbonyLife Media (Nigeria) Abudu has built EbonyLife from a television network into one of Africa’s most ambitious independent media companies, spanning film and television production, talent development and entertainment. She began her media career as the host of pan-African talk show Moments With Mo , launching her own network, EbonyLife TV, in 2013 and film production company EbonyLife Films the following year. EbonyLife was the first African company to sign a multititle deal with Netflix, with Blood Sisters becoming Netflix’s first Nigerian Original series. Abudu has since expanded her international partnerships with companies including Sony, Lionsgate, the BBC and Westbrook Studios. Her brick-and-mortar efforts include the EbonyLife Creative Academy in Lagos, which offers free training on filmmaking and media content production, and the entertainment and lifestyle resort EbonyLife Place. On Oct. 8, Abudu will open EbonyLife Place London, a cinema, restaurant and music/art venue to showcase African talent. Says Abudu: “Talent is everywhere, but opportunity, capital and ownership are not. I think about how we create a future where African storytellers are not just telling our stories but owning them, financing them and taking them to the world.” Maria Pia Ammirati Director, Rai Fiction (Italy) Ammirati has spent more than three decades at Italian public broadcaster Rai, moving from journalism and cultural programming into senior management and becoming one of Italy’s most influential television executives. In a moment when commercial TV is in crisis across Europe, public broadcasters are leading the way both technologically, investing in online and mobile production and distribution, and creatively: Rai Fiction’s fall slate includes an ambitious period drama about the rags-to-riches Panini family publishing empire and the comedy crime series A Small Formality , which is focused on millennials, an overlooked demo in traditional TV. “Audience tastes evolve, as do the social context, technologies and the ways in which people engage with stories,” says Ammirati. “What concerns me most is the increasing tendency to delegate creative processes to technology, with the risk of gradually losing direct contact with the reality we are called upon to portray. It is a challenge we can address and overcome only by ensuring that the human factor remains at the heart of the creative process.” Nadine Bilke Chief Content Officer, ZDF (Germany) A trained journalist who earned her doctorate researching the quality of crisis and war reporting, Bilke joined the German public broadcaster in 2002 and spent much of her early career building ZDF’s digital journalism operation. She became head of ZDFneo in 2018, helping position the channel for younger, digitally oriented audiences, before becoming program director for the parent broadcaster in 2022. Responsible for programming for a nation of 84 million, Bilke says the one thing she worries about “is the growing fragmentation of our societies. We have more content, more platforms and more ways to engage than ever before, yet it is becoming harder to create shared experiences and a common cultural conversation.” Marie-Philippe Bouchard President and CEO, CBC/Radio Canada Bouchard took over CBC/Radio-Canada in January 2025, assuming the tricky role of running Canada’s public broadcaster as linear television shrinks, U.S. streamers dominate Canadian TV, and President Trump’s tariff war and 51st state taunts drive a rise in Canadian patriotism. That’s a bonus for a major broadcaster with a mandate to offer local news, current affairs programming and homegrown TV series coast-to-coast. Bouchard came to the job from TV5 Québec Canada, the French-language broadcaster, where she served as president and CEO from 2016-24. Renata Brandão CEO, Conspiração Filmes (Brazil) Brandão joined Conspiração Filmes in 2006 after studying international relations and communications and completing film-industry studies at UCLA, initially as a production assistant before moving into planning and business management. She became president of business in 2015 and CEO in 2017, helping transform one of Brazil’s best-established independent production companies into an increasingly international operation. Brandão also has expanded Conspiração’s television business beyond Brazil, including into Spanish-language production in Mexico. In 2017, she also founded Hysteria, a Conspiração label focused on stories centered on women. “The obsession with relying strictly on ‘proven IP,’ remakes or hyper-calculated formulas has led to widespread audience fatigue across platforms,” she says. “I would love to see the industry return to trusting producers, creators and instinct over predictive metrics.” From left: Renata Brandao, Mo Abudu and Maria Pia Ammirati Assunta Servello; Courtesy of Subject (2) Amelia Brown CEO, Fremantle U.K. It just made sense when Brown was appointed Fremantle U.K. CEO in 2023: The industry veteran has been with the company for more than 20 years, instrumental in such early hits as Britain’s Got Talent and The X Factor and later Too Hot to Handle for Netflix and Mamma Mia! I Have a Dream for ITV. At the top of the food chain, Brown leads the corporate strategy for one of Britain’s most prolific production outfits and oversees the output of every Fremantle U.K. label. Carol Choi Executive VP, The Walt Disney Co. (Asia-Pacific) Choi’s remit spans both sides of Disney’s Asia-Pacific ambitions: bringing its Hollywood franchises to regional audiences and building a slate of homegrown streaming originals. A Disney veteran since 2006, she previously ran the company’s Japan and Korea businesses and now oversees studios, original content strategy and integrated marketing across the region. With a significant ramp-up of Disney+’s production of international originals now underway, she points to the work of teams in Japan, Korea and Australia as a particular source of pride this year. “From Perfect Crown to A Shop for Killers season two, Battle of Fates and The One Shot , it’s clear that great local stories can stand proudly alongside our most iconic global franchises,” she says. Priya Dogra CEO, Channel 4 (U.K.) Dogra was named CEO of the British broadcaster in December, taking over from Alex Mahon. Her résumé was substantive: She joined Comcast-owned Sky in 2024 as its chief advertising, group data and new revenue officer, having worked at Warner Bros. Discovery and its predecessors for 14 years. At Channel 4, she’s undoubtedly inherited one of the trickiest jobs in the biz — the cash-strapped PSB must adapt or die — and in September unveiled a raft of cuts, she said, part of C4’s “long-term transformation strategy.” Cécile Frot-Coutaz CEO, Sky Studios; Chief Content Officer, Sky (U.K.) The Sky Studios boss actually had her role expanded following Dogra’s departure to Channel 4 and now oversees its advertising division, too. Frot-Coutaz’s remit was already vast — she leads the development, production and commissioning of all of Sky’s original programming, including such record-breaking titles as the Emmy-nominated The Day of the Jackal and the risky SNL UK spinoff. More recently, she’s championed the Dominic West and Sienna Miller-led War , set to dominate our screens this autumn, and played a crucial role in that enormous, billion-dollar ITV-Sky sale. Frot-Coutaz also supervises Sky Studios Elstree, Sky’s state-of-the-art film and TV studio, plus Sky Studios’ global portfolio of production companies that includes Blast! Films, Jupiter Entertainment, True North and Love Productions. Jay Hunt Creative Director of Worldwide Video, Europe, Apple (U.K.) The British Film Institute chair has continued to deftly straddle two enormous jobs in European film and TV. At Apple TV, she’s been pivotal in its transition from middle of the pack to streamer to beat, having championed some of the platform’s biggest global hits, most notably the Emmy-winning Slow Horses , which just scored an eighth season, the BAFTA-winning Bad Sisters and enduringly popular The Buccaneers . Among Hunt’s most anticipated upcoming commissions are Will Sharpe’s magnum opus, Prodigies , and Juno Temple’s starry comedy-drama The Husbands . Jay Hunt (left) and Minyoung Kim Pip/Apple; Courtesy of Subject Angela Jain Head of Content, Disney+ EMEA (U.K.) Jain is overseeing a unit that includes the likes of Rivals , Extraordinary and Stephen Graham’s A Thousand Blows , three huge shows that helped score Disney+ a record 15 BAFTA TV Award nods in March. Before joining the Disney+ team last year, Jain had commissioning stints at E4 and ITV2, where she was responsible for some of the biggest British shows, including Misfits and The Inbetweeners . At ITV Studios, she oversaw big-hitters Love Island and I’m a Celeb . Under Jain, the EMEA team is “ramping up” production across Europe, with regional commissions including the Venice-premiering Oasis documentary and Italy’s Murder on Lake Garda . Ekta Kapoor Joint Managing Director, Balaji Telefilms (India) More than three decades after co-founding Balaji, Kapoor remains one of Indian television’s defining hitmakers. Her revived family soap Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi 2 has topped ratings charts this year, underscoring the enduring pull of her franchises. But the veteran producer also is finding new outlets for her signature serial storytelling. Balaji’s long-term creative partnership with Netflix, announced last year, marked a push to develop projects across multiple formats. In September, she made another significant move: a YouTube partnership for five premium scripted shows spanning 200 episodes. Kapoor will lead the creative direction, with Balaji retaining the underlying IP while tapping YouTube’s global distribution and advertising business — a savvy expansion that doesn’t involve surrendering ownership of her stories. M-K Kennedy Managing Director Worldwide Television, StudioCanal (France) Kennedy has built a career around taking local television production global. A native of Bucaramanga, Colombia, she began in Washington, D.C., producing the Hispanic Heritage Awards before moving to Telemundo, where she helped establish Telemundo Studios Mexico. After seven years at Universal Television and UCP in Los Angeles, she joined Netflix, where she built production teams across Latin America and Europe and oversaw major local-language productions including Money Heist , Dark , Lupin and All Quiet on the Western Front . Last year, Kennedy took charge of StudioCanal’s newly reorganized Worldwide Television division, overseeing the French giant’s international TV drama slate that includes several film-to-series spinoffs drawing from StudioCanal’s vast library. There’s A Prophet (from the 2009 Jacques Audiard prison drama), Apollo Has Fallen (based on the Gerard Butler action franchise) and Army of Shadows , a reimagining of Jean-Pierre Melville’s 1969 film about the French resistance in World War II that is set to star Paddy Considine, Kit Harington, Susan Sarandon and Olivia Colman. Minyoung Kim VP Content, Netflix, APAC (excluding India) For the executive who greenlit Squid Game , Netflix’s most watched series of all time, the bar for a good year is unusually high. But Kim, who is approaching her 10th anniversary at Netflix in November and has overseen the bulk of the streamer’s output in the Asia-Pacific region, has yet another global hit to celebrate. Korea’s Teach You a Lesson recently joined the streamer’s all-time top 10 for non-English television. According to Netflix, APAC content now accounts for more than half the titles in its global non-English Top 10, up from about 30 percent in 2021, while annual worldwide viewing hours for content from the region have quadrupled since 2019. This year’s slate stretches from Thailand’s The Evil Lawyer to Japan’s Plastic Beauty and Australia’s My Brilliant Career alongside a push into live programming with events including BTS: The Comeback and Skyscraper Live . “We’re always looking for the magic of something unexpected that captures the imagination and gets people excited,” she says. “Doing that once or twice is hard work, doing that constantly across nine APAC countries is enough to give anyone insomnia. But, when we get it right, it’s the best feeling in the world.” Anna Marsh CEO, StudioCanal; Member of Canal+ Board; Canal+ Group Chief Content Officer (France) Marsh has spent more than two decades building an international career in film and television sales, distribution and production, rising from international sales at Tele Images and TF1 International to the top of leading French major StudioCanal in 2019. She joined the management board of parent Canal+ in 2022, becoming deputy CEO, and is now also chief content officer for the entire group, putting her undeniably among the most powerful and influential figures in global entertainment with a remit that extends beyond TV to awards-worthy cinema, including this year’s fall festival favorites Elsinore with Andrew Scott and Danny Boyle’s Ink with Jack O’Connell. Under Marsh, StudioCanal has continued to expand its European production and distribution footprint, taking a controlling stake in Italian distributor/producer Lucky Red and Nordic outfit SAM Productions and, at the Canal+ level, signing a new three-year partnership with British pay TV giant Sky that will see the companies develop and co-finance at least two premium English-language dramas a year. Closer to home, Canal+ has announced a French version of Saturday Night Live set to launch this year. Carolyn McCall CEO, ITV (U.K.) Carolyn McCall Courtesy of ITV Has anyone had a busier year than McCall? She negotiated the biggest international TV deal of the year — the 1.6 billion-pound ($2.12 billion) sale of ITV’s broadcasting and streaming business to the Comcast-owned Sky — and handled the aftermath with cool-as-a-cucumber self-assurance. “The announcement of the sale … was a defining moment for ITV,” McCall said on a call with journalists as the company unveiled 2 percent revenue growth in the first half of the year. Unfazed by the prospect of regulatory approval hurdles, McCall (who noted it was ITV who instigated the sale) and her team will be responsible for the most formidable British media group the U.K. has ever seen. Sky would acquire ITV’s networks and streaming businesses (Media & Entertainment) — including the ITV channel portfolio and ITVX — while ITV Studios, the production outfit behind such franchises as Love Island , Britain’s Got Talent and the Netflix hit Fool Me Once , is to be spun off as a standalone listed company, McCall has confirmed. “The competition is ferocious,” she said at a Royal Television Society event in London in September. “It’s not just [being] bigger; it’s also the investment. So you have to invest in technology. You’ve got to continue to invest in AI. You’ve got to continue to invest in efficiency and, most importantly, you’ve got to have enough money to constantly invest in content because content is where it’s at. That’s what makes you all your money.” She has certainly delivered on her promise since taking up the post in 2018, when she vowed to launch a new strategic vision — “more than TV” — in a bid to help ITV adapt to the rapidly evolving media landscape. Her experience spans the top jobs at several of Britain’s leading businesses, including EasyJet and the Guardian Media Group. Beverley McGarvey President, Network 10 (Australia) Twenty years after joining Network 10, McGarvey oversees a portfolio stretching from such free-to-air staples as MasterChef Australia to Paramount+’s full slate of local originals, including NCIS: Sydney and the true-crime series Who the Hell Is Hamish? She says the company’s free streaming service is having its “biggest year yet,” while innovative recent partnerships with such brands as LG and TikTok — the latter aimed at bringing new audiences to Big Brother — have begun to offer fresh avenues to viewers. Keeping Australian production viable amid rising costs and fragmenting audiences remains her priority. “My challenge is creating efficiencies to keep investment flowing into our local content,” she says. One show she wishes she had made over the past year? Disney+’s Rivals . “I just love the escapist, compelling juiciness of the stories,” she says. Anna Marsh (left) and Beverley McGarvey Benjamin Decoin/CANAL+; Courtesy of Subject Anne Mensah VP Content, Netflix (U.K.) Netflix has invested an eye-watering 4.45 billion pounds ($6 billion) in U.K. productions since 2020, creating more than 50,000 jobs in the process. It’s not a stretch to say Mensah and her team have spent well — the buzziest projects among the streamer’s British TV slate continue to overperform across the globe, among them Heartstopper , Adolescence , Black Doves and The Gentlemen . And that’s before you get to the Kate Winslet-Maxine Peake two-hander ( The Unheard ), the untitled Roald Dahl adaptation and the Barry Keoghan-led Top Boy prequel. Cathy Payne CEO, Banijay Rights (U.K.) This year, it was confirmed that Payne would be steering the ship of Banijay Entertainment’s global distribution business following the $8 billion megamerger with All3Media. She’s remained in her post as CEO of Banijay Rights, too, with the Aussie-born executive overseeing the sales of such colossal hits as Survivor , Big Brother and MasterChef , as well as Black Mirror and Peaky Blinders worldwide. Kate Phillips Chief Content Officer, BBC (U.K.) Phillips’ lengthy BBC experience primed her for the CCO role at Britain’s top broadcaster: She was director of unscripted from May 2022 and before that commissioned more than 500 hours of original programs a year, including the still massively popular Strictly Come Dancing and The Graham Norton Show. Now, she’s responsible for all BBC network TV and radio output. Says Phillips, “I’m continually thinking about how we reach audiences who are consuming media on so many different platforms now while still retaining the attribution to the BBC.” Lindsay Salt Director of Drama, BBC (U.K.) Salt is literally behind every single success out of the BBC’s behemoth drama division: Richard Gadd’s Baby Reindeer follow-up, Half-Man ; the long-awaited second season of The Night Manager ; and Sally Wainwright’s Riot Women . She is also the commissioner on some impossibly huge international co-productions, including the BBC and Netflix’s Lord of the Flies and the BritBox phenomenon The Other Bennet Sister (the biggest U.K. drama launch — across all platforms and streamers — this entire year). This is but a fraction of her work platforming original voices, and Salt’s eye for savvy storytelling keeps the BBC’s reputation for prestige drama in tip-top shape. Monika Shergill VP Content, Netflix (India) Netflix’s 10th year in India has given Shergill plenty to celebrate. According to the streamer, India became its largest contributor to non-English film viewing globally in the first half of 2026, while the crime thriller Taskaree: The Smuggler’s Web became the first Indian series to debut at No. 1 on its global non-English TV chart. Her slate’s breadth also is unmatched by global companies operating in the country, spanning the military drama Operation Safed Sagar , the reality series Lock Upp: Sach Ya Sazaa and the Tamil film Made in Korea . “I’m proudest of the range we’ve brought to audiences,” she says. But amid shifting viewing habits, she notes she’s focused most on the nuances within India’s vast viewership: “In a market as diverse as ours, the challenge isn’t scale; it’s specificity for different types of audiences.” Christine Strobl Program Director, ARD (Germany) Strobl has spent her career at the intersection of public service broadcasting and German television drama. A lawyer by training from an impressive family (her father is conservative political icon Wolfgang Schäuble, former president and longest-serving member of the German Parliament), Strobl joined regional public broadcaster SWR in 1999 and rose through programming roles, becoming head of the broadcaster’s film and family programming in 2011. In 2012, she moved to ARD subsidiary Degeto Film as managing director, where she oversaw the development, acquisition and co-production of fiction for the public broadcaster and fought the channel bosses to secure financing for the most expensive German drama of all time: Babylon Berlin . Backed by ARD and pay TV network Sky, Babylon was an early example of Strobl’s push toward cross-channel cooperation, something she’s extended to sports (ARD and streamer Magenta shared rights to matches at this year’s World Cup) and entertainment (the network is seeking a partner to join forces, and share costs, for the broadcast of the next Eurovision Song Contest ). Her favorite non-ARD show of the year was Netflix’s German spy thriller Unfamiliar . “The story itself, with all its twists and turns, is the real star,” she says. “It’s exactly what German fiction can be: high-quality, surprisingly directed and thus internationally appealing.” Christine Strobl (left) and Monika Shergill ARD/Jens Koch; Courtesy of Subject Karen Thorne-Stone President and CEO, Ontario Creates (Canada) As head of the Canadian province’s media investment agency, Thorne-Stone finances everything from feature films to XR content. That role now means navigating industry contraction and uncertainty and ensuring Hollywood producers keep coming to Ontario for tax credits, local talent and varied locations. “There is no end to the talent in our province and country, and we have an extraordinary capacity to fuel growth, jobs and investment if we maintain an environment where creators and businesses can thrive,” she tells THR about her province staying competitive with rival locales. Jane Turton Deputy CEO, Banijay Entertainment (U.K.) Turton is entering a new chapter after steering All3Media for a decade as the company completed its $8 billion megamerger with Banijay this year to create the undisputed indie production and distribution champ. The globe-spanning group with 130 production companies across 25 countries boasts a content catalog that includes The Traitors , Big Brother , MasterChef , Peaky Blinders and Midsomer Murders . The deal marks the end of the All3Media brand, but for Turton, it’s the start of a new chapter. “Leading All3Media has been a huge pleasure and privilege,” she said after the merger closed in July, adding that the combination of the two indie powerhouses would multiply future opportunities “many times over,” bringing together the capacity to deliver “brilliant shows developed and produced by world-class talent” with “the strength of a global distributor, a market-leading digital studio and a growing live events business.” Kylie Watson-Wheeler Senior VP and Managing Director, Disney Australia & New Zealand / head, ESPN APAC (Australia) With The Artful Dodger in production on a third season, Watson-Wheeler, among her many achievements, now has Disney+’s first homegrown Australian streaming hit. She calls the renewal “a rare achievement and a strong marker of the show’s appeal both locally and internationally.” The veteran exec oversees Disney’s Australia and New Zealand businesses and ESPN across Asia-Pacific. After bringing ESPN onto Disney+ in the two countries last year, she has another milestone to celebrate in 2026: the recent successful launch of Disney+ with ads, the streamer’s first ad-supported tier in Asia-Pacific. “Our ad-tier momentum is strong, with sustained acquisition growth and strong engagement,” she says, pointing to opportunities to attract both advertisers and cost-conscious viewers with the platform’s growing mix of live sports, Hulu programming and Disney’s deep library. Profiles by Patrick Brzeski, Lily Ford, Scott Roxborough and Etan Vlessing. This story appeared in the Oct. 7 issue of The Hollywood Reporter magazine.

title: Mike Ditka, No-Nonsense Chicago Bears Legend and TV Analyst, Dies at 86
full_text: Skip to main content By Ira Kaufman Plus Icon Ira Kaufman View All October 9, 2026 8:28am Mike Ditka Rich Pilling/Diamond Images/Getty Images Mike Ditka, the Hall of Fame tight end, Super Bowl-winning coach of the Chicago Bears and TV analyst whose gruff “Iron Mike” style was parodied on Saturday Night Live , has died. He was 86. “It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather and friend, Mike Ditka,” his family said in a statement. “While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach and leader of the Chicago Bears’ Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family. Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.” Related Stories Lifestyle Serena Williams Says Her New Barbie Doll Proves a Girl Can 'Become Anything She Chooses' General News Michael Kearns, Actor, Activist and 'Jerker' Director, Dies at 76 No cause of death was announced. Ditka had a minor stroke in 2012 and suffered heart attacks in 1988 and 2018. “The thing about me,” he told Rick Telander in April 2019, “is that people didn’t think I had a heart. Now they found out I got one.” Emerging from Carnegie, Pennsylvania, a manufacturing community five miles southwest of Pittsburgh, Ditka coached the Bears from 1982-92, guiding the 1985 team to a Super Bowl rout of the New England Patriots 22 years after winning an NFL championship with Chicago as a standout player. The cigar-smoking Ditka said his “Iron Mike” nickname derived from his upbringing in a steel town, but his brusque manner and short temper contributed to his tough image. He became a larger-than-life character, whether he was sticking a wad of gum on a photographer’s camera lens or berating a referee behind his trademark sunglasses. His persona was so large that he inspired a recurring sketch on SNL in the early ’90s known as “Bill Swerski’s Superfans.” Created by Robert Smigel and Bob Odenkirk, the skit had several Chicago sports fans (played by Smigel, George Wendt , Joe Mantegna, Mike Myers, Chris Farley, et al) sitting around a table at Ditka’s sports bar, drinking, smoking and gorging themselves on assorted meats while extolling the greatness of “Da Bears” and the Windy City’s other teams. The faithful wore dark sunglasses and thick mustaches as a homage to their hero, a member of the College and Pro Football halls of fame. Ditka himself appeared twice on SNL and on other shows including Cheers (he was seen on the bar’s TV in the final episode in 1993), L.A. Law , 3rd Rock From the Sun , Entourage , Becker and According to Jim . And in the 2005 film Kicking & Screaming , he’s asked by Will Ferrell’s character to help coach a kids soccer team. “I eat quitters for breakfast and I spit out their bones,” he tells the youngsters . In a 2015 interview, an amazed Ferrell recalled that during filming, Ditka’s hip “popped out” after recent replacement surgery, but he was able to make it through his scenes with just a couple of Advil. He was born Michael Dyczko in Carnegie on Oct. 18, 1939, the son of a welder. The family’s Ukrainian surname was changed to Ditka. He was recruited by 40 schools coming out of Aliquippa High and chose the University of Pittsburgh to stay close to home and pursue a career in dentistry. He was a three-sport star at Pitt, also excelling in baseball and basketball. (The Panthers retired his No. 89 in football, and he was enshrined in the College Football Hall of Fame in 1968.) The Bears selected Ditka fifth overall in the 1961 draft, and he won Rookie of the Year honors after catching 58 passes and scoring 12 touchdowns, extraordinary numbers for a tight end in that era. Ditka’s signature play as a pro came late in the 1962 season, two days after JFK’s assassination. With the Bears trailing the Steelers 17-14 in the fourth quarter, Ditka caught a short pass and broke eight tackles before collapsing to the turf after a 63-yard gain that set up the tying field goal. After the 1966 season, Ditka was embroiled in a contract dispute with Bears owner/head coach George Halas, whom he publicly ridiculed for “throwing nickels around like they were manhole covers.” Mike Ditka with Will Ferrell in the 2005 movie ‘Kicking & Screaming.’ Courtesy of Photofest Ditka was traded to the Philadelphia Eagles in 1967 before joining the Cowboys two years later. His four seasons in Dallas were highlighted by a touchdown catch against Miami in the 1972 Super Bowl, helping Tom Landry and the Cowboys win their first NFL title. Landry hired Ditka as an assistant coach in 1973, and he spent nine years on Landry’s staff as Dallas captured three NFC titles and won another Super Bowl. Ditka was named head coach of the Bears in 1982, reuniting with Halas. He coached them for 11 seasons, posting a 106-62 record and leading Chicago to seven playoff berths. The 1985 Bears, widely considered among the most dominant teams in NFL history, went 15-1 during the regular season before trouncing three playoff opponents by a combined 91-10 margin. Ditka and defensive coordinator Buddy Ryan clashed often about strategy and which man deserved more public recognition for the team’s success. Quarterback Jim McMahon wore a headband and adopted a rebel stance while Hall of Fame running back Walter Payton led a powerful attack. William “Refrigerator” Perry, a 335-pound defensive tackle, became a household name when Ditka used him as a running back in short-yardage situations. That strategy would soon turn controversial. Perry ran for two scores during the 1985 regular season and bulled over for a 1-yard touchdown in the 46-10 Super Bowl rout of the Patriots. Payton did not score against New England and held a grudge about what he deemed an oversight on Ditka’s part. Years later, the coach said he regretted that Payton, whom he lauded as the best player in NFL history, did not reach the end zone during the league’s showcase game. NBC hired Ditka as an analyst on NFL Live after his dismissal from the Bears following a 5-11 season in 1992. He was lured by the Saints to return to the sidelines in 1997, but that turned out to be a mistake. New Orleans went 6-10 in each of Ditka’s first two years, and he made NFL history by trading all of the team’s draft picks in 1999, plus a first-round choice in 2000, to move up and select University of Texas running back Ricky Williams. Ditka later posed for a magazine cover with the Heisman Trophy winner, who was wearing a wedding dress. After the ’99 Saints suffered their 10th loss in 11 games, Ditka suggested to reporters that the Saints would be better off without him. He stuck it out to the end of a 3-13 season before he was fired yet again. Ditka joined CBS Sports as a studio analyst on The NFL Today following his dismissal from the Saints and later appeared as an ESPN commentator on a variety of platforms. He described himself as an “ultra-ultra-ultra conservative” and was a strong supporter of Donald Trump during the 2016 presidential campaign. Some of his political views espoused while he worked for ESPN triggered controversy as Ditka criticized Colin Kaepernick’s protests and stated his belief that “there has been no oppression in America for the last 100 years.” That remark prompted a rebuke from legendary quarterback Joe Namath, who suggested that Ditka needed to look up the word “oppression.” A columnist from the Chicago Sun-Times labeled Ditka “a white man who is blind to the plight of people of color in this country.” In 2020, he became the owner and chairman of the X League, a tackle football circuit for women that was once known as the Lingerie Football League. Survivors include his second wife, Diana, and his four children, Michael III, Mark, Megan and Matthew. Ditka had little sympathy for players who didn’t work hard enough to reach their potential, a subject he addressed during his 1988 enshrinement speech at the Pro Football Hall of Fame. “In life, many men have talent, but talent in itself is no accomplishment,” he said. “Excellence in football and excellence in life is bred when men recognize their opportunities and then pursue them with a passion.” THR

title: Danny Boyle Says ‘28 Years Later: Part III’ Is Currently On The “Back Burner”
full_text: Skip to main content By Zac Ntim Zac Ntim International Reporter @ZacharyNtim More Stories By Zac Danny Boyle Says ‘28 Years Later: Part III’ Is Currently On The “Back Burner” TIFF Lightbox Sets Animation Season Guest Curated By Masaaki Yuasa Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc ‘Dependence’ Back Home To London — LFF View All October 9, 2026 8:20am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Ralph Fiennes in '28 Years Later: The Bone Temple' Miya Mizuno/Sony “It’s on the back burner at the moment,” Danny Boyle concluded this afternoon during a Q&A at the London Film Festival when asked about the current status of 28 Years Later: Part III . The veteran British filmmaker continued to say he “hopes” the film will be made if financing can be locked in. Boyle added that the pause in the film series has also been prompted by Alex Garland’s busy schedule. “Alex has been off doing his own film, which is a huge project,” Boyle said. Alex Garland is currently working on A24’s big-screen adaptation of the hit video game Elden Ring. Related Stories News 'NAZA' Producer James Wilson Addresses "Hysterical, Vituperative" Israeli Government Backlash Against Directors News Grace Harper Brighouse On Bringing Her Camden Film Festival-Winning Doc 'Dependence' Back Home To London -- LFF Boyle is at the LFF this year with his latest feature Ink , which screens as one of the festival’s headline galas. Directed by Boyle from a screenplay written by James Graham (Dear England), the film charts the rise of the UK’s notorious tabloid newspaper The Sun in the 1970s under the editorship of Larry Lamb, after he was poached from the Daily Mirror in 1969 by then budding media mogul Rupert Murdoch. Watch on Deadline Boyle told the LFF crowd that he and his producing team felt specific “pressures” while trying to finance Ink. “We found it very difficult to raise the money for this,” Boyle said. “I have no idea why. They didn’t say why they wouldn’t give us the money. We managed to get the money from StudioCanal. They didn’t give us enough money, but they were brave, whereas a lot of people wouldn’t give us the money.” Boyle said his personal theory about why StudioCanal coughed up the money for Ink is because his producer, Tessa Ross, previously worked on the box office hit Conclave with the company. “She’d made them so much money,” Boyle said, adding he was very lucky that “StudioCanal hooked up with Netflix and they bought it for America. They’ve been really good partners because there have been pressures.” Boyle said he will next work on an Antarctica-set film if he can raise the budget. “That’s the next priority,” he said. The LFF runs until October 18. title: Court TV Parent Law & Crime Ups Rachel Stockman To CEO; Founder Dan Abrams To Remain As Chairman
full_text: Skip to main content By Dade Hayes Dade Hayes Business Editor @dadehayes More Stories By Dade Skydance Shares Rebound After David Ellison And Top Execs Ring Opening Bell At New York Stock Exchange Joe Rogan Sets Multi-Year Extension With Spotify Eyeing More ‘Minecrafts’ And ‘Fallouts’, Microsoft Xbox Launches XP Unit To Take Properties Beyond Video Games View All October 9, 2026 8:17am Add us as a Google Preferred Source Rachel Stockman, CEO of Law & Crime and Court TV Courtesy Rachel Stockman , longtime president of Court TV parent Law & Crime, is becoming CEO of the company as founder Dan Abrams steps down from the role. Abrams, chief legal analyst for ABC News, is staying on as chairman of Law & Crime. The company has been owned since 2023 by Jellysmack , a holding company for creator-led media businesses. Court TV, a digitally focused revival of the longtime cable TV mainstay known for gavel-to-gavel trial coverage, was sold by E.W. Scripps to Law & Crime earlier this year. Related Stories Executives Paramount-WBD Deal Architect Gerry Cardinale Says Most Of $6B In Expected Cost Savings Will Not Be From Layoffs Executives Ex-Mattel CEO Ynon Kreiz In Line For High-Level Paramount Exec Post Stockman has been at Law & Crime for more than a decade, initially serving as editor-in-chief before a promotion to president. Along the way, she has also executive produced dozens of documentaries and series for Netflix, Paramount+, A&E, Fox Nation and HBO Max/ID. Earlier this fall, she oversaw the launch of “Partners in Crime,” a programming initiative featuring six original series developed with some of true crime’s most-followed creators. Watch on Deadline After spearheading the acquisition of Court TV, Stockman has built Law & Crime into a top true-crime brand. It operates four FAST channels and multiple subscription channels on YouTube, which have collectively generated billions of video views and more than 700 million hours watched across platforms over the past year, according to the company. “Rachel’s ability to direct the business at the highest level while also making so many smart, granular decisions has helped lead us to where we are today,” Abrams said in a statement. “She has truly earned this. I can’t wait to see where she takes us next.” Stockman praised the “extraordinary team” at Law & Crime. “I’m honored to lead this next chapter as we continue to push boundaries, embrace bold ideas and help shape the future of media,” she said.
